key_insight: Compress each highly informative frame into a single token at the final LLM layer, keeping essential temporal information while reducing token load by orders of magnitude.
problem_solved: Scales vision–language models to long videos by addressing token explosion and context-length limits that force sparse, temporally fragmented perception.
method: Highly selective frame selection: score and pick a small set of informative frames (learned scoring or attention-based selection).
Extreme per-frame compression: encode each selected frame into one compact token via a lightweight encoder + pooling/distillation so it fits the LLM context.
Temporal preservation & integration: add positional/temporal embeddings and a small aggregator so the LLM receives an ordered sequence of one-token-per-frame representations.
impact: Enables efficient, low-memory long-video reasoning with fewer tokens and faster inference, making VLMs practical for minutes-to-hours videos while retaining temporal cues for downstream tasks.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram: long video frames with a few highlighted (selected) frames mapping to single-token icons.
Architecture schematic: frame encoder → single-token output → positional embedding → LLM input pipeline.
Bar chart: token count, memory and latency comparison (dense frame tokens vs. one-token-per-frame) across video lengths.
Sequence visualization: how temporal order is preserved (tokens with time-stamps) and used by the LLM to produce answers.
paper_title: One Token per Highly Selective Frame: Towards Extreme Compression for Long Video Understanding
paper_authors: Zheyu Zhang, Ziqi Pang, Shixing Chen, Xiang Hao, Vimal Bhat
